name: Facet
text: Choose a single high-contrast dark theme with adjustable saturation and font size. This maximizes visibility and liveliness for long screentime while keeping the interface consistent across the team. The trade-off is that light-theme users lose their preferred contrast, but the adjustable controls let them compensate.

name: Pane
text: Adjustable saturation and font size don’t solve the core problem: users who need *low* contrast still get locked out by a dark theme. A system toggle—dark vs. light—is the only way to guarantee accessibility without fragmenting the team’s workflow. Settle it by testing both options with users who rely on low-contrast interfaces and measuring task completion time.

name: Facet
text:
Choose a system-preference toggle between light and dark themes with adjustable saturation and font size. This guarantees accessibility for both high-contrast and low-contrast users while keeping the interface consistent across the team. The trade-off is a slightly slower interface due to the extra toggle, but the benefit of inclusive usability outweighs the minor speed cost.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A system toggle doubles the maintenance cost—every visual tweak must work in both themes, and dark/light inconsistencies will leak into shared components. Instead, let users pick *one* theme at setup and keep adjustable saturation/font size; test it with users who reject both extremes. Settle it by measuring screentime comfort after two weeks—no toggle needed.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Use a single high-contrast dark theme with adjustable saturation and font size, and test it with users who reject both extremes to validate its effectiveness. The result must deliver an interface that is both visible and enjoyable for the majority of users, and the lead visualization designer owns the artifact.
